Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Assessment summary:
  - Most likely diagnosis: Viral upper respiratory infection / acute bronchitis — based on ~5–6 days of rhinorrhea, continuous dry cough (worse at night), sore throat from coughing, subjective fever/chills, myalgias, marked fatigue, and brief resolved diarrhea. Clinician impression aligned with viral illness.
  - Other considerations consistent with history/DDx:
    - Influenza — systemic symptoms (chills, prominent myalgias, marked fatigue) make this possible (moderate likelihood).
    - COVID-19 — presentation (dry cough, myalgias, subjective fever/chills, transient diarrhea) is compatible (moderate likelihood); no testing documented.
    - ACE inhibitor–induced cough (lisinopril) — plausible contributor given medication and dry nocturnal cough characteristics (medium likelihood) but timing coincided with viral prodrome which favors infectious cause.
- Conflicts/notes:
  - No direct contradictions between transcript and DDx; DDx expanded differential (influenza, COVID-19, ACE inhibitor cough) consistent with transcript details.
  - No objective vital signs or exam findings recorded to confirm fever, respiratory compromise, or alternative diagnosis.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Viral upper respiratory infection / acute bronchitis — High likelihood.
  - Justification: 5–6 day history of rhinorrhea, dry cough worse at night, systemic symptoms (myalgias, subjective fever/chills), brief diarrhea; clinician concluded likely viral.
- Influenza — Moderate likelihood.
  - Justification: Prominent systemic symptoms (shivering, marked myalgias, fatigue) compatible with influenza; no documented high fever or abrupt severe onset to confirm.
- ACE inhibitor–induced cough (lisinopril) — Moderate likelihood.
  - Justification: Patient is taking lisinopril and cough is dry/nocturnal; however, onset concurrent with viral symptoms and systemic features argue toward infectious cause.
- COVID-19 — Moderate likelihood.
  - Justification: Symptoms (dry cough, myalgias, subjective fever, transient diarrhea) are compatible; no testing or anosmia documented.
